title: Derived section functors under an additive equivalence
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal B,\mathcal D$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and assume that $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal B$ have enough injectives [def-sp-enough-injectives]. Let $E:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B$ be an additive equivalence of categories (a functor admitting a quasi-inverse with natural unit and counit isomorphisms). Let $S:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $T:\mathcal B\to\mathcal D$ be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and let $\alpha:S\xrightarrow{\sim}T\circ E$ be a natural isomorphism. For every integer $q\geq0$ there is a natural isomorphism $R^qS\xrightarrow{\sim}(R^qT)\circ E$. For every $X\in\mathcal C$ and every injective resolution $X\to I^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], its component at $X$, under the resolution identifications of both derived functors, is induced on degree-$q$ cohomology by the termwise isomorphism $\alpha_{I^\bullet}:S(I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(E(I^\bullet))$. In degree zero the comparison is $\alpha$.

source.place: Tag 015M, lemma-compose-derived-functors: exact-equivalence special case, combined with the termwise natural isomorphism of the two section functors

proof.text: Fix $X\in\mathcal C$. Choose a monomorphism $s:X\hookrightarrow I^0$ into an injective object. Inductively, after constructing $I^n$, embed the cokernel of the preceding map into an injective $I^{n+1}$, and define $d^n$ as the cokernel projection followed by this embedding. Its kernel is the image of the preceding map, so $0\to X\to I^0\to I^1\to\cdots$ is exact. Put $I^n=0$ for $n<0$. This gives an injective resolution using precisely enough injectives and the kernels and cokernels of an abelian category.

source.place: Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist, proof of (1): successive embeddings of cokernels

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions] to the given additive equivalence $E$. It is exact, preserves injective objects, and sends $s:X\to I^\bullet$ to the injective resolution $E(s):E(X)\to E(I^\bullet)$. Thus $E(I^\bullet)$, without any further replacement, is a permitted resolution for computing $R^qT(E(X))$. The same lemma sends every augmented resolution map $u$ to the augmented resolution map $E(u)$.

source.place: Tag 015M, lemma-compose-derived-functors, proof with F=E and G=T; preservation of injectives from homology.tex Tag 015Z, lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives

proof.text: For every differential $d^n:I^n\to I^{n+1}$, naturality of $\alpha$ gives $T(E(d^n))\circ\alpha_{I^n}=\alpha_{I^{n+1}}\circ S(d^n)$. Hence the components $\alpha_{I^n}$ form an isomorphism of complexes $a_I:S(I^\bullet)\xrightarrow{\sim}T(E(I^\bullet))$; the inverse is termwise $\alpha_{I^n}^{-1}$ and satisfies the chain equation by multiplying the displayed equality by the inverses. The complexes are defined because additivity preserves zero maps, so the consecutive differentials still compose to zero. Taking the kernel modulo the image in degree $q$ gives inverse maps $H^q(a_I)$ and $H^q(a_I^{-1})$.

source.place: Tag 015M, proof, displayed calculation on G(F(I)); the supplied natural isomorphism identifies the two termwise functors

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] for $S$ on the resolution $I$, and for $T$ on the resolution $E(I)$ from step 2. Write their resolution isomorphisms as $i_I:R^qS(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(S(I))$ and $j_I:R^qT(E(X))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(T(E(I)))$. Define $c_X^I=j_I^{-1}\circ H^q(a_I)\circ i_I$. Every factor is an isomorphism, so $c_X^I$ is an isomorphism. Its expression under these resolution identifications is exactly $H^q(\alpha_{I^\bullet})$, as required by the component clause.

source.place: Tag 015M, lemma-compose-derived-functors, proof on an injective resolution; right-derived resolution computations as in Tag 05TD, lemma-left-exact-higher-derived

proof.text:
Let $f:X\to Y$ and choose an injective resolution $J$ of $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists] there is a chain map $u:I\to J$ with $u^0s_X=s_Yf$. Step 2 gives the lift $E(u)$ of $E(f)$. Naturality of $\alpha$ on every $u^n$ gives $T(E(u))\circ a_I=a_J\circ S(u)$ and hence the same square on degree-$q$ cohomology. The map formula of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift], applied once to $S,f,u$ and once to $T,E(f),E(u)$, says
$$i_J\circ R^qS(f)=H^q(S(u))\circ i_I,\qquad j_J\circ R^qT(E(f))=H^q(T(E(u)))\circ j_I.$$
Substitution into the preceding square and cancellation of the isomorphisms gives $R^qT(E(f))\circ c_X^I=c_Y^J\circ R^qS(f)$. No functorial choice of chain lifts is needed: the cited map formula identifies their cohomology maps with the fixed derived-functor maps.

source.place: Tag 013P, lemma-morphisms-lift, (2), and Tag 015M, lemma-compose-derived-functors, natural comparison computed on resolutions

proof.text: For any other injective resolution $J$ of the same $X$, take $f=\mathrm{id}_X$ in step 5. The lift exists by [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists], its image under $E$ is again an augmented lift by [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions], and both derived-functor maps are identities by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift]. The equation proved there is therefore $c_X^I=c_X^J$. Thus $c_X$ is independent of the resolution. Choosing a resolution for each object gives a family independent of all those choices; the equation of step 5 makes it a natural transformation $R^qS\to(R^qT)\circ E$. Since every component is invertible, their inverses also satisfy naturality (multiply that equation on both sides by the inverse components), giving the asserted natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 015M, lemma-compose-derived-functors; independence and functoriality of resolution computations, Tag 013P

proof.text: For $q=0$ and a resolution $s:X\to I^\bullet$ as in step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] (2), applied to $S$ on $s$ and to $T$ on $E(s)$ (an injective resolution vanishing in negative degrees by step 2), gives isomorphisms $\sigma_I:S(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(S(I^\bullet))=\ker S(d^0)$ and $\tau_I:T(E(X))\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(T(E(I^\bullet)))=\ker T(E(d^0))$, induced by $S(s)$ and $T(E(s))$. Put $\theta^S_X=i_I^{-1}\circ\sigma_I:S(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R^0S(X)$ and $\theta^T_{E(X)}=j_I^{-1}\circ\tau_I$. These do not depend on $I$: for another resolution $J$ and the lift $u$ of $\mathrm{id}_X$ of [lem-weil-pbc-injective-resolution-lift-exists], $u^0s_I=s_J$ gives $H^0(S(u))\circ\sigma_I=\sigma_J$ (maps into a kernel are determined after composing with its inclusion), and $i_J=H^0(S(u))\circ i_I$ by [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-map-via-lift] with $h=\mathrm{id}_X$; likewise for $T$ with $E(u)$. The same two facts for an arbitrary $f$ with its lift $u$ show $\theta^S$ natural; these are the natural identifications $R^0S\cong S$, $R^0T\cong T$ of [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], made explicit. Naturality of $\alpha$ at $s$ reads $\alpha_{I^0}\circ S(s)=T(E(s))\circ\alpha_X$; composing with the kernel inclusions gives $H^0(a_I)\circ\sigma_I=\tau_I\circ\alpha_X$ (no degree-zero boundaries, since the resolutions vanish in negative degrees; left exactness of $S,T$ is used through the cited isomorphisms). Hence $c^0_X\circ\theta^S_X=j_I^{-1}H^0(a_I)\sigma_I=j_I^{-1}\tau_I\alpha_X=\theta^T_{E(X)}\circ\alpha_X$: in degree zero the comparison is $\alpha$.
